messages.author: efb064044f1e1c0f
messages.subject: new version of geom_barbed?
parts:
I´m often in the need of producing black/white graphs for journals that charge extra for color reproductions. Hence, I´d like to create plots with linetypes similar to the type b plots in regular r-graphics. Can this be done in ggplot2 0.9.3.1?
I´ve used the hack from http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3810927/getting-r-plot-type-busing a large white filled circle and fill on top of this, but I also see that there used to be a geom_barbed in ggExtra that is now deprecated after the new version of ggplot2. Is there plans for implementing a geom that would allow type b plots in ggplot2 as a standard feature?

//M

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: new version of geom_barbed?
parts:
On Sat, Feb 8, 2014 at 4:58 PM, moleps <mol...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi—

I just find the aesthetics of the graph, and especially the legend, prettier without the lines passing through the shapes.

​Yeah, that makes sense. You don't need to plot the points twice to achieve it though--that is only needed make the lines look like they don't connect to the points. To hide the lines going *through* the points you can use shapes that accept a fill color and set the fill to the same color as the plot background. For example, compare these two graphs:

d <- data.frame(x = 1:10, s = factor(rep(c(1, 2), each = 5)))

p <- ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=x, shape=s, linetype=s)) +
    geom_line()

p + geom_point(aes(shape=s), size = 3) +
    scale_shape(solid=FALSE)

p + geom_point(fill = "gray90",  size = 3) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 25))


Hope this helps,
Ista​

In order to do the legend right I had to dummy code another size scale that was subsequently forced to the same value with a white color and then ensure all the scales had similar labels.



Best,

M

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: new version of geom_barbed?
parts:
The other way to do this (perhaps easier) is to use the point-type
variants that have filled centers (i.e. pch=21:25) and set the fill
colour to the background colour (i.e. white)?

e.g.


d <- data.frame(x=1:5,y=1:5,f=rep(c("a","b"),c(2,3))
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(d,aes(x,y,shape=f,linetype=f))+geom_line()+geom_point(size=3,fill="gray")+
scale_shape_manual(breaks=c("a","b"),values=c(21,22))
